report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/harness.py (lines 281-~480): tier1 aggregation, whole-repo text, repo chunks, BM25 scoring/context, and eval_task_arms. All claims verified against this chunk; most kept, some uncheckable.
risks: eval_task_arms | high | _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS * 4 is used as char cap for B; docstring says 'capped at _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS' (tokens) but code caps by characters, so the actual token count may exceed the nominal cap. | Count tokens of text_b_capped and compare to _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS; if >, claim is broken.

_bm25_context | medium | 'single best-ranked chunk is always included even if it alone exceeds budget' holds only when that chunk is first in the sorted order; if the best chunk is a tie broken by label, it is still first. Claim kept, but verify with a case where the top chunk exceeds budget and a lower-ranked chunk fits. | Construct chunks where top chunk exceeds budget, run _bm25_context, assert it is included.

eval_task_arms | medium | 'budgeted to the SAME token count as A' uses max(tokens_a, 1); if tokens_a is 0, budget is 1, which may not equal 0. Check whether tokens_a can be 0 for a non-error task. | Inspect semantic_slice to see if slice_tokens can be 0; if so, claim is technically broken.

eval_task_arms | low | 'C beats A is tie-inclusive' claim is uncheckable here because recall_c and recall_a are computed but the comparison is not in this chunk. | Find where the comparison is made and verify >=.

eval_task_arms | low | 'never raises' claim is uncheckable for KeyError on task['repo'] because the try block does not catch KeyError; however task is assumed well-formed. Check callers to see if task always has 'repo'. | Inspect task construction in load_minted_tasks or TASKS.

handoff.purpose: Tier1 aggregation, whole-repo text, repo chunks, BM25 scoring/context, and arms A/B/C evaluation.

symbols.name: eval_task_tier1
symbols.note: Aggregates per-task results into tier1 report; handles correctness tasks, resolution errors, focus-withheld, and healthy rows; returns n_tasks, n_primary_tasks, n_quarantine_tasks, n_errored_tasks, n_focus_withheld, focus_withheld_ids, tokenizer, per_task, errored, by_provenance.

symbols.name: _whole_repo_text
symbols.note: Walks repo, concatenates source files with headers; cap_chars=None walks untruncated; returns (text, truncated).

symbols.name: _target_query
symbols.note: Returns BM25 query fallback: symbol after '::' or file stem.

symbols.name: _repo_chunks
symbols.note: Walks repo, extracts units via extract_units, else whole file; returns list of (label, text) with deterministic sorted dirnames.

symbols.name: _bm25_tokenize
symbols.note: Tokenizes text into lowercase identifier tokens.

symbols.name: _bm25_scores
symbols.note: Computes Okapi BM25 scores over pre-tokenized docs; returns list of floats.

symbols.name: _bm25_context
symbols.note: Top-k BM25 retrieval up to budget_tokens; returns dict with text, n_chunks_total, n_chunks_used, truncated, tokens.

symbols.name: _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS
symbols.note: Default model cap tokens for Tier2, value 120000.

symbols.name: eval_task_arms
symbols.note: Deterministic A/B/C comparison for one task: recall and token cost for semantic slice, whole-repo, and BM25; never raises on resolution errors; refuses correctness tasks.

claims.text: No top-level blended recall/compression: see ``by_provenance`` for the honest, per-provenance-tier numbers.
claims.why: The returned dict has no top-level recall/compression keys; only per_task and by_provenance contain such aggregates.

claims.text: ``tier == "quarantine"`` tasks are counted in ``n_quarantine_tasks`` and reported inside ``by_provenance``, but never inside a go/no-go figure.
claims.why: n_quarantine_tasks is computed as n - n_primary; by_provenance is built from healthy which includes quarantine tasks (unless errored/focus_withheld); no go/no-go figure exists in this chunk.

claims.text: A single unresolvable task ... is caught here too, not just inside ``eval_task_tier1``: this loop resolves the repo/builds the index ITSELF ... before calling ``eval_task_tier1``, so that resolution step needs its own guard.
claims.why: The loop calls resolve_task_repo and cached_index inside try/except (ValueError, OSError) before eval_task_tier1, and appends _task_error_row on failure.

claims.text: ERRORED rows land in both ``per_task`` (never silently dropped -- "a degraded measurement is reported, never silent") and the dedicated ``errored`` list, and are excluded from ``by_provenance`` (every mean/recall/compression aggregate)
claims.why: errored rows are appended to per_task; errored list is derived from per_task; healthy excludes rows with 'error', and by_provenance is built from healthy.

claims.text: ``n_tasks``/``n_primary_tasks``/``n_quarantine_tasks`` remain simple total-attempted counts over label alone (unaffected by error status, and therefore byte-identical to before this existed for any store with zero errored tasks); ``n_errored_tasks`` is new and additive.
claims.why: n_tasks is len(per_task) which includes errored rows; n_primary uses _is_primary_tier on label_tier; n_quarantine is n - n_primary; these do not depend on error status. n_errored_tasks is len(errored) and additive.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD (lane A1): the fence fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- not a resolution error (excluded above), not a recall outcome either. Excluded from `healthy` (therefore from every mean/miss count in by_provenance) same as errored rows, and separately counted/named so it is reported, never silently folded into either a pass or a miss.
claims.why: focus_withheld list is built from per_task rows with 'focus_withheld'; healthy excludes them; n_focus_withheld and focus_withheld_ids are returned.

claims.text: ``cap_chars=None`` (the new default) walks the ENTIRE repo untruncated -- the TRUE size of the baseline.
claims.why: When cap_chars is None, the if cap_chars is not None condition is never true, so no truncation occurs and the loop returns all files.

claims.text: Pass an int to cap it (what Tier 2 actually hands a model). Returns (text, truncated); ``truncated`` is always False when uncapped.
claims.why: When cap_chars is not None, truncation sets truncated=True; when None, truncated is initialized False and never set True.

claims.text: BM25 query fallback when a task has no ``question``: the target symbol name, or the file's stem for a file-level target.
claims.why: If '::' in target, returns part after '::' (symbol name); otherwise returns stem of path (file stem).

claims.text: Retrieval units for arm C: one chunk per extractable unit (function or class), else the whole file when nothing is extractable -- "the repo's files/units" the BM25 baseline retrieves over.
claims.why: Uses extract_units; if units exist, appends one chunk per unit; else appends whole file text.

claims.text: Same source-file universe as ``_whole_repo_text``.
claims.why: Both use os.walk, filter _IGNORE_DIRS and dot-dirs, use spec_for to filter files, and read with same encoding/errors.

claims.text: Unlike ``_whole_repo_text``, dirnames ARE sorted here: this is new code with no prior byte-order contract to preserve, and BM25 tie-breaking needs a deterministic candidate order (see ``_bm25_context``).
claims.why: _repo_chunks sorts dirnames with sorted(); _whole_repo_text does not sort dirnames (only filenames).

claims.text: Standard k1=1.2 / b=0.75.
claims.why: Default parameters are k1=1.2, b=0.75.

claims.text: Ties are broken by the CALLER (chunk label, not insertion order) so retrieval order stays deterministic regardless of dict/set iteration order (PYTHONHASHSEED).
claims.why: _bm25_scores returns raw scores; sorting with label as secondary key is done in _bm25_context.

claims.text: Top-k BM25 retrieval up to ``budget_tokens`` -- arm C. Chunks are taken whole, never split mid-chunk; the single best-ranked chunk is always included even if it alone exceeds budget (an empty context is a strictly worse baseline than a slightly-over one).
claims.why: The loop breaks only when picked is non-empty and total + t > budget; the first chunk is always appended regardless of budget.

claims.text: ``truncated`` is True iff a lower-ranked chunk existed that did not fit the remaining budget.
claims.why: truncated is set True only when a chunk is skipped due to budget; if all chunks fit or no chunks remain, it stays False.

claims.text: A = the distilled semantic slice (today's product).
claims.why: text_a is res['slice_text'] from semantic_slice.

claims.text: B = naive whole-repo concat. Recall is measured against the TRUE, FULL, UNTRUNCATED text (``tokens_B``) -- beating a baseline you truncated is not a win.
claims.why: text_b_full is from _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None), which is untruncated.

claims.text: ``tokens_B_capped_at_default``/``b_truncated_at_cap`` additionally report what Tier 2 would actually hand a model (capped at ``_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS``), so that weakening is visible, not hidden inside a smaller B that looks stronger than it is.
claims.why: text_b_capped is from _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS * 4) and b_truncated_at_cap is returned; tokens_b_capped is computed.

claims.text: C = BM25 top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A (``token_budget_C == tokens_A``) -- the "dumb retrieval" baseline that matters commercially.
claims.why: budget_c = max(tokens_a, 1); if tokens_a > 0, budget_c == tokens_a; the max only changes when tokens_a is 0, which is an edge case.

claims.text: ``c_beats_a`` is TIE-INCLUSIVE (``recall_C >= recall_A``, matching the report's "C>=A" column and this module's own docstring promise that a tie is "reported loudly, not smoothed over") and reported plainly either way; nothing here is tuned to make A win.
claims.why: The comparison recall_C >= recall_A is not present in this chunk; only recall_c and recall_a are computed. The tie-inclusive behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: same per-task resolution guard as ``eval_task_tier1`` -- a ``ValueError``/``OSError`` resolving the repo or slicing the target returns an ERRORED row (``_task_error_row``) instead of propagating.
claims.why: The try block catches (ValueError, OSError) from resolve_task_repo, cached_index, _repo_chunks, and semantic_slice, returning _task_error_row.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is likewise refused (``_correctness_task_row``) rather than scored: all three arms here go through ``_recall``, so a task with no ``must_include`` would read as a perfect 1.0 in every arm at once.
claims.why: The function checks is_correctness_task(task) at the start and returns _correctness_task_row(task).

observations.what: The cap for B in eval_task_arms is _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS * 4, but the docstring says 'capped at _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS'. The cap is in characters, not tokens, so the actual token count may exceed the nominal cap.

In _bm25_scores, the IDF formula uses math.log(1.0 + (n - c + 0.5) / (c + 0.5)). This is a standard BM25 variant, but the docstring does not specify the exact formula; it is a claim about 'standard' being kept.

In _bm25_context, the first chunk is always included even if it exceeds budget, but if the first chunk is not the best-ranked (due to tie-breaking by label), the 'single best-ranked chunk' claim could be off. However, the sort ensures the best score with label tie-break is first, so it is the best-ranked.

In eval_task_tier1, the try block catches only (ValueError, OSError). If task['repo'] is missing, a KeyError would propagate, contradicting 'never silently dropped' but the docstring says 'unresolvable task (bad repo label)' which implies a present but invalid repo. The claim is kept for the stated exceptions.
